moduleTitle: Lesson 5 - Connecting Tosca to TMA: TCPs, Local vs Remote
learningObjectives: Configure the test configuration parameters (TCPs) that connect Tosca to a TMA instance.
Validate connection values against the documented format without assuming a single universal failure cause.
Set up a genuine Local vs Remote topology, including the correct TMA startup flag for Remote.
Separate device visibility, network reachability and successful session creation during diagnosis.

elements.term: The same TCP mechanism used elsewhere in Tosca
elements.description: TCPs configure test environments on supported Tosca objects. Child objects inherit values and can override them; Configurations bundle reusable TCP values.

elements.title: Key TCP values
items: TMAServer — the Agent address; follow the documented connection format and topology.
DeviceName — selects a specific target or uses the documented TOSCA_DYNAMIC_DEVICE_SELECTION value for dynamic selection.
LiveView — True enables a screenshot preview during local-device execution; it is not a continuous video recording guarantee.
Browser — ChromeAndroid or SafariiOS for the corresponding hybrid/mobile web scenario.
AppiumServer — specifies the Appium endpoint for the chosen connection or cloud provider; capabilities and compatibility still matter.
ScreenFlow and ScreenFlowPath — configure both for saved screenshots of Input TestStepValues.

bulletPoints: TCP inheritance and lower-level overrides apply to mobile configuration.
Use the parameters required by the selected platform, application and connection.

elements.description: Specify the verified device identifier to target one device. Availability and successful connection still need checking; pinning an identifier does not guarantee a run will start.

Use TOSCA_DYNAMIC_DEVICE_SELECTION for the documented dynamic selection mechanism. It is not an arbitrary wildcard in DeviceName. Dynamic selection does not by itself enable parallel execution or guarantee coverage of every matching device.

elements.text: Choose a specific identifier for device-specific reproduction. Configure supported selection and parallel-execution settings separately when using a device pool.

bulletPoints: A pinned target supports reproducibility when available.
Dynamic selection and parallel execution are separate settings.

elements.text: The documented Remote (TMA) address format ends with a slash: http://<ip_address>:<port_number>/. Use the configured endpoint and port. This format alone does not prove how every version builds URLs or explain a particular session error.

A successful scan is useful evidence, but does not prove that the execution uses the same effective configuration. Compare inherited TCPs, selected device, endpoint and session logs rather than assuming a universal scanning-versus-execution parsing difference.

bulletPoints: Compare effective scan and execution configuration before assigning a root cause.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Local vs Remote, set up for real

elements.description: In a local setup, the Agent and Tosca run on the same host. Some locally connected scenarios do not require explicit TMAServer or DeviceName values; check the platform-specific requirements.
In a remote setup, the Agent and Tosca run on different computers. For TMA 2025.4 iOS hosting, follow the macOS support matrix rather than assuming all older host descriptions remain supported.

elements.text: The documented remote CLI setup uses start --rest-address <IP>:<port>. Configure the Appium endpoint separately with its own port; reaching the web interface alone does not prove an automation session can start.

elements.title: Example: Mac running TMA, Windows running Tosca Commander
items: On the Agent host, locate the installed Agent executable and use the documented remote start command for that operating system.
Configure the actual remote endpoint, target identifier and other required TCPs in Tosca. Do not assume the REST bind port equals the Appium port.
Verify connectivity from the Tosca execution host and inspect Agent/session logs with a minimal test.

bulletPoints: Remote CLI setup binds the REST service with --rest-address.
Validate the automation endpoint from the execution host, not only on the Agent machine.

elements.term: Use evidence from each connection layer
elements.description: A device listed in the Agent is discovery evidence, not proof that application launch, driver setup, session negotiation and network routing all work. Record the failed operation and logs before assigning responsibility.

elements.title: A systematic diagnostic order
items: Verify that the intended device is connected, prepared and not occupied.
Check the effective TCPs and the configured REST and Appium services.
Test endpoint reachability from the actual execution machine, including relevant routing and firewall rules.
Run a minimal session/application-opening test and use logs to isolate the failure.

bulletPoints: Device discovery does not certify a working automation session.
Investigate configuration and networking according to the failing layer.

examPitfalls.title: Treating the address format as a complete root-cause diagnosis
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Scan succeeds and execution fails, so the team assumes a specific URL parsing defect without examining logs.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the documented address format, compare effective configuration and inspect the failure. The symptom alone does not identify its cause.

examPitfalls.title: Starting Remote TMA from the tray icon
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Launching TMA normally on a second machine, confirming its console is reachable in a browser from the Tosca machine, and assuming remote mode is active.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the documented remote CLI binding and verify the actual automation service from the execution host; web-interface visibility alone is insufficient.

examPitfalls.title: Jumping straight to network troubleshooting on a connection failure
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a firewall or proxy issue the moment a TMA session fails to start, without first checking the TCP values.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check effective configuration and reachability from the execution host. Do not claim most failures are malformed TCPs or postpone relevant network checks without evidence.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Remote (TMA) address form matches the documented format, assuming the correct host and configured port?

options.text: A local APK file path only

practiceQuiz.hint: Provide the scheme, host, configured port and documented slash.
practiceQuiz.rationale: B matches the documented remote endpoint form. Using that form does not by itself prove session readiness or diagnose all connection errors.

optionExplanations.A: A bare address omits the documented URL structure.
optionExplanations.B: This follows the remote URL format with the actual configured port.
optionExplanations.C: BundleID selects an iOS app, not the Agent endpoint.
optionExplanations.D: An APK path identifies an installation build, not the endpoint.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the correct way to start TMA for a Remote (TMA) setup?

options.text: Double-click the tray icon on the remote machine.
Run tricentis-mobile-agent start --rest-address <IP>:<port> from the command line on the machine hosting TMA.
Open the TMA console in a browser from the Tosca machine.
No special startup is needed — TMA is remote-capable by default.

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the documented CLI binding on the Agent host.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The remote connection guide uses start --rest-address <IP>:<port>. Verify the required automation endpoint and reachability separately; opening the console is not a complete remote setup.

optionExplanations.A: Launching the tray is not the documented remote binding command.
optionExplanations.B: This is the remote CLI command in the Agent guide.
optionExplanations.C: Console access alone does not establish the configuration.
optionExplanations.D: Remote service binding must be configured and verified.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The Agent lists the device as connected and idle, but execution cannot create a session. What is the best next investigation?

options.text: The device — it must be reconnected.
Compare effective TCPs, endpoint reachability and session logs without assuming the device is fully healthy.

practiceQuiz.hint: Discovery is not end-to-end session evidence.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Connection and idle state narrow the investigation but do not rule out driver, app, network or configuration failures. Use the failed-session evidence instead of assigning blame from discovery alone.

optionExplanations.A: Discovery alone does not show that reconnecting is needed.
optionExplanations.B: These checks distinguish discovery from successful session creation.
optionExplanations.C: The symptom does not establish a cellular-carrier problem.
optionExplanations.D: The symptom does not isolate the USB cable.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TCP value tells Tosca which specific device, emulator, or simulator to target?
practiceQuiz.hint: TMAServer points at the agent; this one points at the specific target.
practiceQuiz.rationale: DeviceName selects the target device or supported selection mode. TMAServer identifies the Agent; LiveView enables the local execution preview.

optionExplanations.B: This enables a local execution preview.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the documented Local (TMA) connection type, which component manages the device connection for Tosca?
practiceQuiz.hint: BrowserStack and Perfecto are cloud device-farm providers, not the local connection layer.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TMA manages devices for this connection type. Cloud providers offer different connection options; underlying Appium functionality does not replace the Agent in the specified Local (TMA) setup.

optionExplanations.A: This is a cloud provider, not the specified local component.
optionExplanations.B: Appium supplies underlying automation functionality; the specified connection is Local (TMA).
optionExplanations.C: The named connection uses the Mobile Agent.
optionExplanations.D: This is a cloud provider, not the specified local component.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team owns supported, idle local devices and manages their access securely. Which three potential operational benefits can this setup provide? (three correct answers)

options.text: Control over the in-house test environment
Automatic access to rare devices the team does not own
Direct access to the owned, idle hardware
Avoiding a remote device-farm network hop

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the stated availability assumptions; ownership does not add missing devices.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The stated setup provides environment control, direct access and no remote-farm hop. These are potential benefits, not guaranteed security or overall speed; ownership does not add unowned models or remove the automation driver.

optionExplanations.A: The team controls the stated in-house environment.
optionExplanations.B: The team cannot access unowned rare models merely by using local hardware.
optionExplanations.C: The scenario explicitly supplies owned, idle hardware.
optionExplanations.D: Local ownership does not remove the underlying automation connection.
optionExplanations.E: The stated local setup avoids a remote-farm hop, without guaranteeing total speed.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which device allocation approach is best for consistent testing on a specific device?
practiceQuiz.hint: Which approach pins DeviceName to one exact device, run after run?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A specific identifier selects the intended device when available. Dynamic selection is appropriate for a pool, but does not guarantee that one particular device is chosen.

optionExplanations.A: Dynamic selection may choose a different target.
optionExplanations.B: A specific identifier supports the stated device-specific goal.
optionExplanations.C: A virtual target does not itself pin the required device.
optionExplanations.D: Sharing does not itself pin the required target.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following statements about Test Configuration Parameters (TCPs) in Tosca Mobile are true? (three correct answers)

options.text: The DeviceName TCP supports both static and dynamic configurations
The Browser TCP specifies browser settings for hybrid apps on Android and iOS
The generic AppiumServer TCP is used only for BrowserStack configurations
TOSCA_DYNAMIC_DEVICE_SELECTION is the documented DeviceName value for dynamic selection

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish the documented selection value from provider-specific endpoint details.
practiceQuiz.rationale: DeviceName supports specific and dynamic selection; Browser configures hybrid/mobile web context. AppiumServer is not restricted to BrowserStack. Dynamic selection uses the documented value rather than an arbitrary wildcard.

optionExplanations.A: Specific and documented dynamic selection are supported.
optionExplanations.B: Browser chooses the hybrid/mobile web context for the platform.
optionExplanations.C: The endpoint parameter is not limited to one named provider.
optionExplanations.D: This is the documented dynamic-selection value.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the primary purpose of TCPs in Tosca Mobile?

options.text: To define and customize mobile test execution settings
To store test execution results in external databases
To replace test cases with predefined test scripts
To limit the number of test cases that can be executed

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what TMAServer, DeviceName, LiveView and ScreenFlow have in common.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TCPs configure the execution environment and behavior; they do not replace TestCases or act as a results database.

optionExplanations.B: They are not a results database.
optionExplanations.D: They do not define a universal case-count cap.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TCP enables Tosca Mobile to capture and store screenshots automatically during test execution?
practiceQuiz.hint: Two of these are a pair — one switches the feature on, the other only says where the files land.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ScreenFlow enables saved Input TestStepValue screenshots when configured with ScreenFlowPath. LiveView provides an execution preview; ScrollToVisible concerns control steering.

optionExplanations.A: This supplies the storage path rather than enabling the feature alone.
optionExplanations.B: This enables saving when paired with the path parameter.
optionExplanations.C: This enables preview, not the screenshot-storage feature.
optionExplanations.D: This concerns scrolling a control into view.

quickRecap.value: TCPs configure environments with inherited values and lower-level overrides.
Use the actual Agent endpoint and a verified target identifier.
Pin a target for device-specific work; use TOSCA_DYNAMIC_DEVICE_SELECTION for documented dynamic selection.
Use ChromeAndroid or SafariiOS for the relevant hybrid/mobile web context.
Configure the Appium endpoint for the selected connection/provider; compatibility still matters.
Follow the documented remote URL format without assuming a particular failure mechanism.
Use the documented --rest-address remote command and configure the Appium service separately.
Device listing is discovery evidence, not proof of full session health.
Compare configuration, execution-host reachability and session logs.
Configure ScreenFlow and ScreenFlowPath together for saved Input TestStepValue screenshots.
